subject: A very common question about Reproducible Shiny app

messages.author: 6d6db76cac37a1b0
messages.subject: A very common question about Reproducible Shiny app
parts:
Hi Joe Cheng and other Shiny developers, 

I have a question about R Shiny reproducibility. I have created a Shiny app doing linear regression model, basically, when users finish their analysis, they can download a report, which is designed as a Rmarkdown file.

However, my question is that is there a way to capture/store variable selections from users' last set of analysis? If so, next time when users want to check their analysis outputs, they do NOT have to go through exactly the same variable selections again. 

Any insight will be highly appreciated. 

Thank you so much!

parts:
Hi Joe, 

Thank you so much for such a quick reply. The package shinyURL is definitely on my list of research. 

Another possibility that I'm aware of so far is .rds file (which can store different R objects). Basically, I can save user selections as sub-lists in the .rds file, and refer to the corresponding element next time when user upload this .rds file. I think this way works; however, manually code/save each selection as a sub-list (in .rds) means a lot of work to me. So have you any better ideas on this option?

Thank you.

I saw a presentation from Susan Holmes in Sydney in December last year. She said that her research group was working with RStudio on a solution for this problem. It would be available in Shiny in a future release.

ShinyURL has some bad restrictions, such as requiring you to use short variable names. It makes code maintenance harder.

messages.author: dea7fe9fc1920d2f
messages.subject: Re: A very common question about Reproducible Shiny app
parts:
Hi all,

I can not share code unfortunately, but what's working for me quite fine is a redis database as backend to store user settings.

Each control is built in server.R using renderUI, fetching previous settings per user from redis via rredis if available. Each control is accompanied by an observer which stores each user setting immediately as a single key/value pair in redis. Performance and user experience ist great. You can close an app any time, open it again and continue your work at the exact state you left it. There is no noticeable delay from the redis access.

Implementation can get a bit tricky if there are complex dependencies between controls - it's difficult to control the order of the initialization in shiny.

Hope this helps

Thomas
